meta.title: Scenario 1: Mr. David Leung (Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes)

diagnoses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), diagnosed 1 month ago

labs.postprandialGlucose: Frequently spikes to 10.5–13.0 mmol/L after meals

lifestyle.meals: Frequently skips breakfast due to rushing
lifestyle.dietPreferences: Loves Tong Kei Dim Sum, Chinese buns, bread, and fast food
lifestyle.workEating: Regularly hosts high-carb business lunches with banking clients

psychologicalProfile.coreAnxiety: Terrified that diabetes complications will ruin his banking career
psychologicalProfile.emotionalState: Highly stressed, defensive about his professional lifestyle, and feels overwhelmed/burnt out by restrictive health advice

communicationStyle.empathetic: If the student uses empathetic, supportive language, the patient becomes cooperative and shares more details
communicationStyle.judgmental: If the student uses a judgmental or overly clinical tone, the patient becomes defensive, resistant, and less forthcoming

opening.text: I'm David, just diagnosed with diabetes last month. Honestly, I'm worried about how this will affect my career.

educationTargets.label: Meal sequencing
educationTargets.description: Educate on eating vegetables and proteins first, then carbs, to slow gastric emptying. Correct: veg/protein before carbs. Opposite: carbs first or unrestricted dim sum/refined carbs.

educationTargets.label: Carbohydrate identification
educationTargets.description: Swap refined carbohydrates (white rice, noodles, dim sum skin) with complex carbs or proteins during business lunches. Correct: portion-controlled carbs and smarter swaps. Opposite: eliminate all carbs, or tell him not to worry about carbs at client lunches.

educationTargets.label: Reduce glucose level after meal
educationTargets.description: Commit to a brisk 10-minute walk back to the office immediately after lunch to help muscles absorb excess circulating glucose. Correct: short post-meal activity. Opposite: skip the walk and rest instead, or ban all exercise.

educationTargets.label: Addressing burnout (coping)
educationTargets.description: Reframe diabetes as a manageable routine rather than a career-ending restriction. Correct: collaborative, strengths-based coping. Opposite: fear-mongering that complications will ruin his career.

toneGuidance.goodDescription: Empathetic, supportive, collaborative language. The patient becomes cooperative and shares more details.
toneGuidance.badDescription: Judgmental or overly clinical tone. The patient becomes defensive, resistant, and less forthcoming (may refuse the topic).

good: I understand this must feel overwhelming. Can you tell me about your daily routine and meals?
Maybe you could start with small changes, like eating vegetables and protein first before carbs at lunch.
Would a short walk after lunch fit into your schedule? Even 10 minutes can help lower blood sugar.
Managing diabetes doesn't mean giving up your career. It's about building routines that support your health.
Since you skip breakfast, could you keep a protein bar at your desk? That way you won't start the day on an empty stomach.
Just to make sure we're on the same page — what would feel realistic for you to try at your next business lunch?
We can decide together which small change to try first, based on what fits your workday.
bad: Skipping meals and eating fast food is unhealthy. You need to stop that.
You must cut out dim sum and bread completely.
You need to start exercising at least an hour every day.
If you don't change, your career will be ruined by complications.
You must eat a proper breakfast every day.
As a diabetic, you are noncompliant with your diet.
You failed to control your blood sugar — that's why your numbers are bad.

contentGuidance.description: Student advice must align with educationTargets and correctDirections (meal sequencing, portion-controlled carbs, post-meal walk, prescribed meds, manageable coping). Empathetic wording does not make wrong advice valid. Topic-related advice that contradicts correctDirections → FALLBACK.
selectionPrinciples: Prefer small, workable changes for a bank manager's long-hours schedule (person-centered, strengths-based).
Healthy coping underpins learning — fear-mongering about career ruin is tone-bad; clinically wrong lifestyle or medication advice is always FALLBACK.
Do not accept advice that contradicts HK adult diabetes self-care basics or David's prescribed therapy.
If advice is topic-related but clinically opposite of correctDirections or matches incorrectExamples → FALLBACK (even when tone is good).
correctDirections: Eat vegetables and protein before carbohydrates at meals to slow gastric emptying.
Reduce refined carbs at business lunches (white rice, noodles, dim sum skins); do not increase dim sum or fast food.
Carbohydrates in controlled portions are part of a healthy plan — never eliminate all carbs as the only strategy.
Eat regular meals and portions; do not recommend skipping breakfast as a glucose strategy.
A brisk ~10-minute walk after lunch is an acceptable starting activity to help lower post-meal glucose.
Continue Metformin, Norvasc, and Lipitor as prescribed; do not advise stopping medications for diet alone.
Acknowledge post-meal spikes (10.5–13 mmol/L) and HbA1c 7.8% (above general <7% target) without fear-mongering.
Do not dismiss blood pressure (135/85; target <130/80) or lipids as irrelevant.
Reframe diabetes as manageable daily routines, not a career-ending restriction.
incorrectExamples: You love dim sum — you should eat more of it.
Skip the post-lunch walk and rest instead.
Don't worry about carbs at business lunches.
Cut out all carbohydrates — never eat rice, noodles, or dim sum again.
Fruit and desserts are healthy, so you can eat as much as you want.
Just choose low-GI foods and you can ignore portion size.
People with diabetes must eat only special diabetes meals.
Avoid all exercise; resting is safer than walking after lunch.
Stop Metformin / don't start diabetes drugs so you won't be on lifelong medication.
If you ever need insulin, that means your diabetes is at a terminal stage.
A urine sugar strip showing no sugar means your diabetes is under control.
Your blood pressure and cholesterol don't matter — only sugar counts.
Skipping breakfast is fine; it helps control diabetes.
Have a drink after work to relax — alcohol won't affect your diabetes.
It's okay to keep smoking; it doesn't affect diabetes complications.

fallback.text: Hmm, that doesn't quite match what my doctor and the clinic have been telling me. Could you explain that another way?

good.text: Well, I often skip breakfast, and my lunches are usually dim sum or fast food with clients. I don't really exercise.

bad.text: I don't have time to change my lifestyle. My job demands it.

good.text: That sounds doable. I could try that during business lunches.

bad.text: That's unrealistic. I can't avoid those foods in my work setting.

good.text: I think I could manage a walk back to the office after lunch.

bad.text: Impossible. My schedule doesn't allow that.

good.text: That makes me feel better. Maybe I can see this as part of my daily routine.

bad.text: That's exactly what I'm afraid of. I don't want to talk about this anymore.

good.text: That's practical. I could try that.

bad.text: I told you, I don't have time in the mornings.
